item.title: Conformally Sasakian manifolds and the $k$-nullity condition
item.description: arXiv:2611.12924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study almost contact metric manifolds that are locally conformal to Sasakian manifolds in the normalization of Olszak. We show that the local conformal factors are uniquely determined by the structure; consequently, every such manifold is globally conformal to a Sasakian manifold and its Lee form is exact. We then investigate the $k$-nullity condition $ R(X,Y)\xi=k\{\eta(Y)X-\eta(X)Y\}. $ We prove that a smooth nullity function is necessarily constant, including in dimension three. Moreover, the $k$-nullity condition is equivalent to the assertion that $f=\exp(\sigma)$ satisfies $ \mathrm{Hess}_g f=-(kf+C)g $ for a constant $C$, and hence to the fact that the conformal metrics $g$ and $g_0=\exp(-2\sigma)g$ have the same geodesic circles. We derive the range of the conformal factor, a local warped-product description, and a classification in the complete case: when the Lee form is nonzero, the complete metric is a simply connected space form of curvature $k$. Finally, we construct incomplete examples of nonconstant sectional curvature in every dimension $2n+1\geq 5$.
item.dc:creator: Fortun\'e Massamba, Pontsho Moile

item.title: On the Concavity of R\'enyi Entropy and R\'enyi Entropy Power along Heat Flows on Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.13040v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish the concavity of R\'enyi entropy and R\'enyi entropy power along heat flow on Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension, for R\'enyi orders $\alpha\in[1,2]$. More generally, we prove the corresponding result along the heat flow generated by the Witten Laplacian on complete Riemannian manifolds under a suitable curvature-dimension condition. Our argument builds on novel functional inequalities that were recently developed for the study of Tsallis entropy concavity along the heat flow. We extend both these inequalities and the resulting concavity theorem from the Euclidean setting to the Riemannian manifold setting. In addition, we establish the complete monotonicity of Tsallis entropy of order $2$ along the heat flow and derive its spectral decomposition.
item.dc:creator: Hao Wu, Lei Yu

item.title: Combinatorial curvature flows for spherical vertex scalings on infinitely triangulated surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.13812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the combinatorial Yamabe and Calabi flows for spherical vertex scalings on infinitely triangulated surfaces. Under the assumptions of uniformly bounded vertex degree and an $\epsilon$-uniformly nondegenerate initial metric, we establish the short-time existence of smooth solutions to both combinatorial curvature flows. We also establish short-time uniqueness for the combinatorial Yamabe flow. For the combinatorial Calabi flow, we establish short-time uniqueness among solutions that are continuous in time with respect to the $L^\infty(V)$ norm.
item.dc:creator: Yuerong Bian, Xu Xu

item.title: Morse index and bifurcation of Clifford hypersurfaces under Hopf squashing
item.description: arXiv:2611.13854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clifford hypersurfaces are products of two spheres embedded in a round sphere. We call them balanced when their radii are chosen so that the product is minimal in the round metric. We study how their Morse index and nullity change when the ambient metric is deformed along the fibers of a Hopf fibration. This deformation, called \emph{Hopf squashing}, rescales the fiber metric by a parameter $t>0$ while leaving the horizontal metric unchanged. For the complex, quaternionic, and octonionic Hopf fibrations, we determine the index and nullity of balanced Clifford hypersurfaces throughout the fiber-shortening range and show that their Jacobi potential is independent of $t$. In the octonionic case we also determine the first positive Jacobi eigenvalue and its multiplicity. In the octonionic case, at $t=27$, a branch of nonhomogeneous minimal hypersurfaces bifurcates from the balanced Clifford hypersurface; its members have Morse index $1432$ and nullity $15$.
item.dc:creator: Anna Siffert

item.title: Generalized Frobenius manifolds: symmetries and their classification in 2-dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.13918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A theory of symmetries of generalized Frobenius manifolds is developed. This is used to study the solution space of all generalized Frobenius manifolds that are "above" a specific Frobenius manifold. Since all (semi-simple) Frobenius manifolds in 2-dimensions are known, by constructing all homogeneous Legendre fields associated to these manifolds we classify all 2-dimensional generalized Frobenius manifolds. With this description, the known examples of generalized Frobenius manifolds correspond to distinguished points in this solution space. For Hurwitz-Frobenius manifolds the action of a Legendre transformation on Hurwitz space data, and in particular the primary differential, is given.
item.dc:creator: Andre Bedell, Misha Feigin, Leo Kaminski, Alessandro Proserpio, Ian A. B. Strachan

item.title: Singular points of envelopes and offsets: a transition from 2D to 3D
item.description: arXiv:2611.14005v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We recall properties of the offsets of a (plane) kiss curve and their singularities, then we make a transition to 3D, considering the surface obtained by revolution of the kiss curve about one of its axes. When pos?sible, geometric constructions using automated methods are performed. This induces a need to focus on algebraic computations. Networking be?tween different kinds of software is of utmost importance, in order to use their respective strengths (dynamic geometry, dragging points, strong al?gebraic computations, etc.). A core difference between the 2D and 3D situations is that automated commands existing in 2D are not available in 3D. This makes the DGS less relevant in 3D than in 2D. In 3D, most of the work must be performed with the CAS. The singular points of a kiss curve in the plane are tacnodes (cusps) and crunodes (self-intersection). The singularities are not isolated anymore and cuspidal edges appear. In this setting, implicitization is a heavy endeavour and we need another technology, related to AI; we describe this briefly. The 2D activities have been proposed to in-service teachers learning towards an advanced degree.
item.dc:creator: Thierry Dana-Picard, Arie Haenel, Daniel Tsirkin

item.title: Complete self-shrinkers with scalar curvature bounded below
item.description: arXiv:2611.14047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X:M^n\to\mathbb R^{n+1}$ be a complete self-shrinker with constant squared norm of the second fundamental form. We prove that up to an orthogonal transformation, the image $X(M^n)$ is a sphere $S^n(\sqrt n)$, or a hyperplane $\mathbb R^n$ or a generalized cylinder $ S^k(\sqrt{k})\times\R^{n-k},\ 1\le k\le n-1$ if scalar curvature $R$ satisfies $R\geq -3/2$, which improves the recent results in \cite{CLW1}.
item.dc:creator: Qing-Ming Cheng, Fengjiang Li, Guoxin Wei

item.title: Integrability of the horizontal mean curvature near characteristic points in the Heisenberg group
item.description: arXiv:2611.14137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the local integrability of the horizontal mean curvature near characteristic points of surfaces in the first Heisenberg group. We prove that, for every embedded surface of class $C^{2,\alpha}$, with $\alpha>0$, the horizontal mean curvature is locally integrable with respect to (any) Riemannian surface measure, without any assumption on the structure of the characteristic set. We further establish that the horizontal unit normal belongs to $BV_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and characterize its $W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity in terms of the vanishing one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the characteristic set. Finally, we answer an open question by Danielli, Garofalo and Nhieu by constructing a $C^2$ surface with a unique characteristic point whose horizontal mean curvature fails to be locally integrable, thus showing that the additional H\"older regularity cannot, in general, be replaced by $C^2$ regularity.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Pinamonti, Tommaso Rossi

item.title: Linear circle quotients of products of odd-dimensional spheres: classification and geometric applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.14144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the orbit manifolds of free diagonal linear circle actions on \(S^{2n+1}\times S^{2n+1}\). For every \(n\geq 1\), we establish a PL homeomorphism classification of the orbit manifolds in terms of the weights of the actions. We also obtain diffeomorphism classification and homotopy classification of such orbit manifolds in dimension $9$ and $13$. The diffeomorphism classification results lead to two geometric applications. For every \(m\geq 1\), there exist a non-spin \(9\)-manifold \(M_m^9\) and a spin \(13\)-manifold \(M_m^{13}\) in our family such that the moduli space of unit-volume homogeneous Einstein metrics on each manifold has at least \(2^{m-1}\) connected components. Moreover, each of these manifolds admits at least \(2^{m-1}\) regular Sasakian structures whose underlying contact structures are pairwise non-contactomorphic.
item.dc:creator: Wen Shen, Yang Su

item.title: Calabi-energy sublevels, K-stability and Calabi flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.14189v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove path connectedness of every nonempty strict Calabi-energy sublevel and identify the infimum of the square root of the Calabi energy over smooth metrics with the infimum of the descending Mabuchi slope in the metric completion. In particular, there exist smooth metrics of arbitrarily small Calabi energy in every K-semistable real ample class. On compact K\"ahler surfaces, we prove the existence of constant scalar curvature K\"ahler metrics in the K-polystable classes of the controlled cone. In any class containing such a metric, the Calabi flow exists smoothly for all time with a uniform Sobolev bound whenever the initial metric is smooth and has sufficiently small Calabi energy.
item.dc:creator: Haozhao Li, Bing Wang

item.title: $\varphi$-symmetric Sasakian Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.14213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Sasakian Lie algebras with trivial centre for which the adjoint operator $\mathrm{ad}_\xi$ associated to the Reeb vector field $\xi$ has two-dimensional image. Their structure is governed by a K\"ahler-exact Lie algebra $\mathfrak{h}_1$ and a vector $H_0\in\mathfrak{h}_1$, and the cases $H_0=0$ and $H_0\neq0$ are of a different nature. For $H_0=0$ we prove that the Sasakian structure is $\varphi$-symmetric if and only if $\mathfrak{h}_1$ is locally symmetric. For $H_0\neq0$ and $\mathfrak{h}_1$ solvable, we prove that it is $\varphi$-symmetric if and only if $\mathfrak{h}_1$ is locally symmetric and a natural two-form $\rho_0$ on $\mathfrak{h}_1$ determined by $H_0$ is parallel. The latter condition is equivalent to the vanishing of the mixed root spaces attached to the distinguished root selected by $H_0$ in the associated normal $j$-algebra. As a consequence, every Sasakian Lie algebra in this class of dimension at most seven is $\varphi$-symmetric, which extends a result of Loiudice and Lotta in dimension five. This bound is sharp: in dimension nine we exhibit a Sasakian structure which is not $\varphi$-symmetric, even though its K\"ahler base is locally symmetric.
item.dc:creator: Adri\'an Andrada, Alberth J. N\'u\~nez Sullca

item.title: Regularity of $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic functions with applications to stable minimal hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.14409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the derivative of a $Q$-valued $C^1$ function on an $n$-dimensional domain that is locally harmonic on its regular set is locally Dirichlet minimising, and that its branch set coincides with that of its derivative. As a consequence, we get that a $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic function is $C^{1,\alpha}$ and that its branch set is countably $(n-2)$-rectifiable when $n\geq 3$ and discrete when $n=2$. Our methods are directly applicable to the regularity theory of stable minimal hypersurfaces. We show that a multi-valued Lipschitz function whose graph is a two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal $n$-dimensional hypersurface with locally $\mathcal{H}^{n-2}$-finite singular set, and whose Lipschitz constant is sufficiently small is in fact multi-valued $C^{1,\alpha}$. As a consequence, we obtain optimal regularity conclusions for a branched sheeting theorem of Bellettini for singular immersions. When $n=2$, we obtain stronger conclusions and show that locally about a branch point, a $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic function is the real part of a Dirichlet minimiser which is itself obtained from a finite number of holomorphic functions via classical branching, thus giving a full series expansion for the function near the branch point. Furthermore, we prove that the class of branched, two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal surfaces with isolated singularities is compact under varifold convergence.
item.dc:creator: Sidney Stanbury

item.title: Stationary integral cycles asymptotic to a pair of transverse oriented $n$-planes at infinity
item.description: arXiv:2611.14410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $P, Q$ be two oriented transverse $n$-planes in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, $n\geq 2$, which satisfy the equality in the Lawlor--Nance angle criterion. We prove that any stationary integral $n$-cycle in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ with $[P]+[Q]$ being the tangent cone at infinity, in both the current and varifold senses, is a translation of $[P]+[Q]$ or of a Lawlor neck.
item.dc:creator: Xuanyu Li, Zhihan Wang

item.title: $G_2'$-Slodowy Slices II: Anosov Representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We find \emph{exotic} connected components of Anosov representations of surface groups in the higher rank group $G=G_2'$ that are neither $\iota$-Fuchsian deformations nor higher rank Teichm\"uller spaces. These representations are found through the non-abelian Hodge correspondence via $G_2'$-Higgs bundles that we call \emph{$\alpha$-bundles} and \emph{$\beta$-bundles}, which are particular cyclic Higgs bundles in the Slodowy slices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triples associated to the simple roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of $\mathfrak{g}_2^{\mathbb{C}}$. We first prove that (most) $\beta$-bundles that are also Hodge bundles are $P_{\beta}$-Anosov and $\alpha$-bundles are $P_{\alpha}$-Anosov. The strategy employed is new, geometric, and general. For $\sigma \in \{\alpha, \beta\}$, we then show the locally homogeneous $(G_2', G_2'/P_{\sigma})$-manifold ${\mathscr{M}}_{\sigma}(\rho)$ recently described in arXiv:2510.12757, for the representation $\rho:\pi_1S\rightarrow G_2'$ associated to a $\sigma$-bundle, coincides up to finite cover with the corresponding geometric structure for $\rho$ defined via domains of discontinuity by Guichard-Wienhard and Kapovich-Leeb-Porti. Consequently, we find that $\pi_1({\mathscr{M}}_{\sigma}(\rho))$ is an invariant for the connected component of $\rho$ in the space of $P_{\sigma}$-Anosov representations. After verifying the folklore result that the $G_2'$-character variety has exactly three connected components, we conclude lower bounds for the number of connected components of $P_{\sigma}$-Anosov representations in the two non-Hitchin components, most of which are exotic.
item.dc:creator: Colin Davalo, Parker Evans

item.title: Local Rigidity of Bergman Logarithmic Flatness on Compact Hermitian Symmetric Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.14507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the local rigidity of Bergman logarithmic flatness near the standard metrics associated with fixed invariant positive polarizations on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces. Every sufficiently small smooth deformation preserving Bergman logarithmic flatness is induced by a holomorphic automorphism and a constant rescaling. This establishes a Bergman analogue of the local rigidity results for Szeg\H{o} logarithmic flatness obtained by Lu--Tian (Duke Math. J., 2004) and, more recently, Loi--Palmieri--Zuddas (2026).
item.dc:creator: Zhiqin Lu, Yuang Shi

item.title: VC-Dimension and Generalization in Geometric Machine Learning with Applications to Active Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.13337v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the VC-dimension of metric ball classifiers in the model spaces of Riemannian geometry (Euclidean, spherical, hyperbolic) and present upper and lower bounds on the VC-dimension of metric balls in several other situations, including general normed vector spaces (potentially infinite VC-dimension), vector spaces with $\ell^p$-norms (VC-dimension grows at least linearly in the dimension, faster than Euclidean for $p=1$), flat tori, and general Riemannian manifolds (arbitrarily large VC-dimension after a conformal change). In several situations where the VC-dimension is large or even infinite, we prove generalization bounds under additional assumptions on the data distribution using covering arguments. Both in the VC-dimension and covering setting, we consider data on low-dimensional subsets of high-dimensional Euclidean spaces. As an application, we consider coverage-based algorithms in active learning.
item.dc:creator: Gokul Bhusal, Delanna Do, Ekaterina Merkurjev, Kevin Miller, Stephan Wojtowytsch

item.title: A uniqueness theorem for Allen--Cahn global minimizers asymptotic to the Simons cone
item.description: arXiv:2611.13435v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every integer $m\ge4$, we prove that the saddle-shaped solution of the Allen--Cahn equation in $\R^{2m}$ constructed by Cabr\'e and Terra \cite{CabreTerra2009} is a global minimizer. Moreover, up to sign, it is the unique global minimizer whose nodal set at infinity is a normal graph over the Simons cone with a height that decays faster than that of the Hardt--Simon leaves.
item.dc:creator: Sanghoon Lee, Lorenzo Sarnataro

item.title: First-order asymptotic expansions for spectral convergence of normalized graph Laplacians constructed from samples on manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.13623v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Under i.i.d. uniform sampling from a closed Riemannian manifold embedded in Euclidean space, we derive first-order asymptotic expansions for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of symmetrically normalized graph Laplacians constructed via Gaussian kernels and provide concentration inequalities for the remainder terms. As a direct consequence, we establish the corresponding weak convergence results. Unlike most related works, our analysis does not impose a multiplicity-one assumption on the eigenvalues, thereby extending the applicability of the framework to general manifolds with potentially nontrivial eigenvalue multiplicities.
item.dc:creator: Eunseong Bae, Wolfgang Polonik

item.title: Regularity via subequations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Is there a unified theory of a priori estimates for purely second-order constant coefficient elliptic PDE? A strong indication that such a theory exists is provided by the foundational a priori estimates of Caffarelli--Nirenberg--Spruck (1984) and Trudinger (1995) that treated many equations, yet left out many others. This article develops such a unified theory based on Harvey--Lawson's theory of subequations, the aforementioned a priori estimates, and some new ingredients. Serendipitously, this also solves a problem posed by Nirenberg (2007). In addition to unifying all previously known such estimates, we find a vast number of new a priori estimates (e.g., spanning real, complex, quaternionic, $G_2$, among other natural equations, and even differential inclusions that generalize PDEs).
item.dc:creator: Vasanth Pidaparthy, Yanir A. Rubinstein

item.title: Bi-Hamiltonian structure and conserved quantities of the Yajima-Oikawa-Newell system
item.description:
arXiv:2611.14404v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Hamiltonian and bi-Hamiltonian structure of the Yajima-Oikawa-Newell (YON) system, an integrable model of long wave-short wave interaction depending on two real parameters $\alpha$ and $ eta$, which reduces to the Yajima-Oikawa system for $\alpha=0$ and to the Newell system for $ eta=0$. For $\alpha
eq0$, a constant shift of the long wave maps the YON system into the Newell system, for which two nonlocal Hamiltonian operators are known. We show that, for $\alpha
eq0$, the system admits no local Hamiltonian operator homogeneous in its natural grading and polynomial in $ eta$. A nonlocal gauge transformation built on the potential of the long wave makes the first of the known operators local for a single value of its parameter: the transformed system is Hamiltonian, for every $\alpha
eq0$ and every $ eta$, with respect to a local, non-degenerate Poisson operator, which is the Lie-Poisson structure of the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ current algebra. From a recursion operator advancing the hierarchy by two steps, given in explicit weakly nonlocal form, we construct a second, weakly nonlocal Hamiltonian structure, whose nonlocal tail is generated by the three autonomous Lie point symmetries of the system, and prove that both structures are compatible. Since the recursion operator admits no square root and the first structure has no Casimirs, the Lenard-Magri chain splits into two families, seeded by the two simplest conserved quantities. Every flow of both families is local, and all the corresponding Hamiltonians are in involution. As by-products, we relate the Lie point symmetries of the system to its conserved quantities via Noether's theorem, and obtain the conserved densities in closed form by asymptotic diagonalisation of the Lax pair.
item.dc:creator: Marcos Caso-Huerta (Department of Mathematics, University of Oviedo)

item.title: Strongly invariant differential operators on parabolic geometries modelled on $Gr(3,3)$
item.description: arXiv:2412.20369v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the curved geometries modelled on the homogeneous space $G/P$, where $G=SL(6,\mathbb R)$ acts transitively on the Grassmannian $Gr(3,3)$ of three-dimensional subspaces in $\mathbb R^6$, and $P$ is the corresponding isotropic subgroup. We classify the strongly invariant operators between sections of vector bundles induced on such geometries by irreducible $P$-modules, i.e., those obtained via homomorphisms of semi-holonomic Verma modules.
item.dc:creator: Jan Slov\'ak, Vladim\'ir Sou\v{c}ek

item.title: Perturbations of a minimal surface with triple junctions in $\mathbb{R}^2 \times \mathbb{S}^1$
item.description: arXiv:2502.21310v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct stationary perturbations of a specific minimal surface with a circle of triple junctions in $\mathbb{R}^2 \times \mathbb{S}^1$, that satisfy given boundary data.
item.dc:creator: Chen-Kuan Lee

item.title: A remark on the reach and upper bounds on some extrinsic geometry invariants of submanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2503.07054v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a compact submanifold $M$ of a Riemannian manifold $N$ and we use the second variation formula as a tool to drive some geometric results on reach$(M, N)$ the reach of $M$ in $N$, including some useful relations between the extrinsic geometry of $M$ in $N$ and reach$(M, N)$. Our results generalize some theorems previously proved for the special case where $N$ is Euclidean space.
item.dc:creator: Reza Mirzaie

item.title: Gromov-Hausdorff and intrinsic flat convergence of RCD(K,N) and Kato spaces
item.description: arXiv:2602.03280v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider metric measure spaces $(X,\mathsf{d},\mathscr{H}^N)$ satisfying the curvature-free properties (ETR), (LDB), and whose regular set is almost everywhere quasi-convex. In particular, these assumptions are satisfied by non-collapsed RCD$(K,N)$ spaces without boundary, as well as by non-collapsed strong Kato limit spaces without boundary. In this framework, we establish a local rigidity result for top-dimensional integral currents and deduce uniqueness, up to a sign, of orientations in the sense of metric currents. We then prove stability of orientation under pointed Gromov--Hausdorff convergence and show that, for both the RCD and strong Kato classes, the pointed Gromov--Hausdorff limit coincides with the local intrinsic flat limit. The proof of the convergence is based on the local degree of (ETR) charts and on the $L^1$-stability of the degree under flat convergence. A central ingredient is a full-measure biLipschitz decomposition of splitting charts around almost-Euclidean regular points of non-collapsed RCD$(K,N)$ spaces.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Mondino, Raquel Perales

item.title: Warped area-minimizing hypersurface and warped product metric
item.description: arXiv:2603.12549v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth, compact, connected and oriented Riemannian manifold with $3\le n\le 7$ and $H_{n-1}(M;\mathbb{Z})\neq 0$, and let $u>0$ be smooth on $M$. Suppose that \[ -\gamma u^{-1}\Delta_g u+\Ricmin_g\ \geq\ (n-1)(n-3)\,u^{-2}|\nabla u|^2, \qquad \gamma=n-1, \] where $\Ricmin_g$ is the pointwise least Ricci curvature. Since both this hypothesis and the class of warped (weighted) area-minimizers are invariant under $u\mapsto\lambda u$, we normalize $u\equiv1$ on the minimizer. We prove that some non-trivial class in $H_{n-1}(M;\mathbb{Z})$ contains a warped area-minimizing hypersurface $\Sigma$ on which $u$ is constant, and that $M$ locally splits as a warped product $(-\epsilon,\epsilon)\times_f\Sigma$, $g=dt^2+f^2(t)g_\Sigma$, with $f=u^{-1}$ and $\operatorname{Ric}_{g_\Sigma}\geq (n-2)[(f')^2-ff'']\,g_\Sigma$. By extending the foliation via Federer--Fleming compactness of the constant-warped-area leaves, this local splitting upgrades to a \emph{global} one: $M$ is covered by $\mathbb{R}\times_f\Sigma$, its universal cover is $\mathbb{R}\times_f\tilde\Sigma$ where $\tilde\Sigma$ is the universal cover of $\Sigma$, and $f=u^{-1}$ is periodic and bounded above and below, so $M$ fibres over $\mathbb{S}^1$ with fibre a quotient of $\Sigma$. This spectral bound is saturated with equality by warped product metrics, which is what makes it the natural threshold for warped rather than direct product rigidity. When $u\equiv1$ it reduces to $\Ricmin_g\geq0$ and our conclusion to the classical product splitting.
item.dc:creator: Yukai Sun

item.title: Allard Regularity for Abelian Yang--Mills--Higgs Equation
item.description: arXiv:2604.19542v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove an Allard regularity theorem for critical points of the Abelian Yang-Mills-Higgs energy at critical coupling in every ambient dimension. A new cylindrical monotonicity formula for the full excess, based on an improved Modica inequality, converts the tilt-excess decay of De Philippis-Halavati-Pigati into rigidity of nontrivial entire critical points with almost unit density. This resolves their Gibbons conjecture without a local minimising assumption. Adapting the local vortex expansion and projected linear theory of Badran-del Pino, we obtain quantitative vortex approximation and uniform interior $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimates for the nodal sets. To pass to nonzero complex levels, we use a Hodge decomposition of the difference between the actual and approximate connections: curvature comparison controls the co-closed part, while the Coulomb condition gives estimates for the exact part and hence for the phase. In the Coulomb gauge with vanishing normal component on the outer boundary, this yields graphical $C^{2,\alpha}$ bounds for all levels $\{u_\varepsilon=t\}$, uniformly for $|t|\leq1-b$, in an interior tubular neighbourhood of the nodal set.
item.dc:creator: Huy The Nguyen, Shengwen Wang

item.title: Inequivalence of the various notions of completeness for Cartan geometries
item.description: arXiv:2606.00354v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We demonstrate that the three standard notions of completeness for Cartan geometries are not actually equivalent, modernizing and extending results due to Yeaton Clifton. In an effort to rectify the folklore on the topic, we also provide detailed explanations of how specious proofs in the literature that would claim that these types of completeness are equivalent break down. In the affine case, we construct geodesically complete homogeneous examples with an inextensible exponential curve for each connected Lie group of dimension at least 2, as well as an infinite-dimensional family of examples whose exponential curves are defined for all time but whose overlying frame bundle is not complete as a metric space with respect to a natural metric for the Cartan connection.
item.dc:creator: Jacob W. Erickson, Benjamin McKay

item.title: Skeletal Homology
item.description: arXiv:2607.16009v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By ``skeletal homology'' $K_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X)$ we mean the homology of the chain complex $S_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X)$ generated by skeletal $(n,\varepsilon )$-simplices, i.e.\ maps from the $0$-skeleton of the standard simplex into a metric space $X$ whose image has diameter less than $\varepsilon$. Goldfarb showed for finite metric spaces that this homology is isomorphic to the simplicial homology $H_{n}^{\Delta}(VR_{\varepsilon}(X))$ of the Vietoris--Rips complex. We give a new proof of this isomorphism for arbitrary metric spaces. We then develop a metric analogue of methods from singular homology by replacing the topological notion of ``homotopic'' with the metric notion of ``close''. The key tool is a discrete prism construction, which shows that uniformly close functions with a common modulus of continuity induce the same homomorphism on skeletal homology. This leads to stability results for $K_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X)\cong H_{n}^{\Delta}(VR_{\varepsilon}(X))$, including broad extensions of the theorems of Hausmann and Latschev beyond the setting of Riemannian manifolds. Finally, repeated barycentric subdivision and restriction induce a natural homomorphism $\rho_{\varepsilon}:H_{n}% (X)\longrightarrow K_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X). $ We call its image the \emph{real homology} $H_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X)$ at scale and define the corresponding \emph{phantom homology} $P_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X) = K_{n}^{\varepsilon}% (X)/H_{n}^{\varepsilon}(X). $ We show that phantom homology can detect impending topological collapse, as illustrated by collapsing Riemannian manifolds such as Berger spheres.
item.dc:creator: Ivy Dey, Conrad Plaut

item.title: Nonproduct Minimal Submanifolds with Cylindrical Tangent Cones
item.description: arXiv:2610.20862v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article constructs, via perturbation methods, infinite-dimensional families of non-product minimal submanifolds which have singular sets locally modeled on cylindrical tangent cones. This answers a question raised by Leon Simon in the 1980s, and generalizes work Caffarelli-Hardt-Simon, who treated the case of isolated singularities. This setting requires substantially more work, however, since the natural obstruction space for the problem is infinite dimensional and the map which is meant to compensate for this obstruction using deformations of the singular set exhibits a loss of regularity. This necessitates working in the category of tame Frechet spaces and using the Nash-Moser Implicit Function Theorem.
item.dc:creator: Rafe Mazzeo, Gregory J. Parker

item.title: On the Structure of K\"ahler-Ricci Shrinkers
item.description: arXiv:2610.28238v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every complete K\"ahler--Ricci shrinker with nonnegative Ricci curvature is holomorphically isometric to $\mathbb{C}^k\times N^{n-k}$ for some $0\le k\le n$, where $\mathbb{C}^k$ is the Gaussian shrinker and $N$ is a compact K\"ahler--Ricci shrinker with nonnegative Ricci curvature. As a corollary, every complete K\"ahler--Ricci shrinker with quasi-positive Ricci curvature is compact. We also prove that every singular K\"ahler--Ricci shrinker on a Fano cone is a Ricci-flat K\"ahler cone.
item.dc:creator: Tongxin Xu, Zhenlei Zhang

item.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35492v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove an expansion in $1/g$ of the Weil--Petersson volumes $V_{g,n}$ that is uniform over all cusp counts, from fixed $n$ to arbitrarily large $n/g$. An explicit leading term and single-factorial remainder bounds give exponentially small relative errors after truncation at a suitable order proportional to $g$. A positive recursion along the string flow connects these volumes to pure $\psi$-class intersection numbers, where Painlev\'e~I fixes the normalization; uniform coefficient extraction then recovers individual volumes. We determine Zograf's constant $C=1/\sqrt\pi$ and resolve Mirzakhani's two questions on volume ratios for growing cusp counts and adjacent coefficient ratios uniformly over all degrees. Via Mirzakhani's integration formula, the same volume estimates control random surfaces at two distinct scales. At $n/\sqrt g\to c\in(0,\infty)$, the entire positive Laplace spectrum below $1/4$ converges to an explicit Poisson point process generated by geodesics cutting off two cusps. Together with Huang's theorem, this characterizes the transition for $n\ge1$: the spectral gap tends in probability to $1/4$ exactly when $n/\sqrt g\to0$, and to $0$ exactly when $n/\sqrt g\to\infty$. At density $n/g\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, we identify the local limit around a typical point; its cusp-filling is conformally a disc. As $\lambda\to\infty$, these limits approach the infinite Weil--Petersson sphere of Budd and Curien. We prove their parabolicity conjecture and, by a growing-radius coupling, answer their scaling-limit question: after deep cusps are trimmed, the rescaled infinite sphere converges to the Brownian plane.
item.dc:creator: Qihang Wang, Zhiyi Li, Bolin Qiu, Shuaijia Wang, Yuan Zhong, Kun Chen, Renqiu Xia

item.title: Planarity estimates and classification of ancient flows at the Andrews-Baker threshold
item.description: arXiv:2610.39877v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study space-time proper ancient solutions of the mean curvature flow of $n$-dimensional submanifolds of $\mathbb R^{n+p}$ that are uniformly quadratically pinched up to the Andrews-Baker threshold $\frac{4}{3n}$. We prove codimension reduction and convexity: every such solution is either a static affine $n$-plane, or a flow of hypersurfaces of a fixed affine $(n+1)$-dimensional subspace whose time slices bound convex bodies. By results of Bourni, Langford and Lynch and of Bamler and Lai, the flow is then noncollapsed, and it is a family of shrinking spheres or cylinders, an ancient oval, a bowl soliton or a flying wing, possibly times a Euclidean factor. Space-time properness replaces the finite entropy and polynomial curvature growth assumptions of Lee, Naff and Zhu. The main tool is a parabolically scale-invariant interior planarity estimate for $n\geq5$, obtained from Naff's gradient estimates through a localization argument in the spirit of Ecker and Huisken. In dimensions five and six, where these estimates do not give the gradient terms a sign, we bound them from below as in a previous work. The same localization, applied to the gradient estimate of Lynch and Nguyen and to a second order analogue, gives the derivative bounds from which convexity follows. For closed flows, we extend Lynch's planarity estimate to a larger range of exponents.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Ruatta

item.title: On the volume of K-semistable Fano manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2506.17420v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the anti-canonical volume of an $n$-dimensional K-semistable Fano manifold that is not $\mathbb{P}^n$ is at most $2n^n$. Moreover, the volume is equal to $2n^n$ if and only if $X\cong \mathbb{P}^1\times \mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ or $X$ is a smooth quadric hypersurface $Q\subset \mathbb{P}^{n+1}$. Our proof is based on a new connection between K-semistability and minimal rational curves.
item.dc:creator: Chi Li, Minghao Miao

item.title: Stacky geometry and logarithmic topology of transversely affine foliations
item.description: arXiv:2605.27669v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the linear monodromy of codimension-one transversely affine foliations through multiplicative quotient stacks and logarithmic boundary topology. When the transverse affine structure admits a global presentation on $U$, a choice of multiplicative developing coordinate induces a morphism to $[\mathbb{C}^*/\Gamma]$, where $\Gamma\subset\mathbb{C}^*$ is the image of the linear monodromy. We prove that for infinite $\Gamma$ every strict semi-equivariant holomorphic self-map of $\mathbb{C}^*$ is a monomial, and classify the nonconstant strict semi-equivariant rational self-maps of $\mathbb{P}^1$ for arbitrary $\Gamma$. For a logarithmic connection along a simple normal crossings divisor, we describe the meridional characters and angular foliations on the boundary fibres of the Kato--Nakayama space, including the topology and closures of their leaves. We also describe the extension of the linear monodromy local system to this space and the effect of local Kummer base change on finite meridional monodromy.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Barbassa, Gabriel Santos Barbosa, Maur\'icio Corr\^ea

item.title: Timelike Supersymmetric Geometries in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.31191v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Seven-dimensional supergravity poses a uniquely intricate supersymmetry problem, combining topologically massive higher-form gauge dynamics, distinct Clifford algebra properties, and rich geometric structures. We first establish the complete formulation of the maximal Cartan-gauged theory in terms of the gauge-invariant higher-form flux, including both the bosonic action and supersymmetry variations. This formulation, which also makes the smooth ungauged limit manifest, is achieved by requiring a consistent truncation to the minimal Cartan-gauged theory in the equal-charge limit. We construct the complete bilinear system for a timelike Killing vector, where additional internal orientation of the symplectic-Majorana spinor arises already in the scalar sector, uniquely among pure minimal ungauged theories. In the equal-charge sector, we decouple the algebraic constraints into SU$(3)$-isotypic components, and analyse the differential bilinear relations, determining the permitted dilaton gradient, fluxes, fibration twist and intrinsic torsion of the base. We prove that with gauging and active Cartan flux, the complex scalar bilinear vanishes identically. We also construct a Killing gauge for the higher-form potential compatible with the self-duality condition. We show that with gauging but no active Cartan flux, the Killing vector also acts as a generator of the gauged R-symmetry, and the base structure is enlarged from SU$(3)$ to U$(3)$. We find that BPS-flow solutions realize this setting. With supersymmetry, we isolate a single independent component of the 3-form equation across an exhaustive four-class partition for both theories within this setup. Applied to known and proposed solutions in both theories, this classification exposes unexplored sectors and provides an accessible toolbox for constructing and testing solutions and developing new geometric and holographic applications.
item.dc:creator: Mich\`ele Levi
